purpose: Malathion is used to treat head lice infestations in people 6 years of age and older. It kills both lice and their eggs (nits) that live on the scalp and hair. Your doctor may prescribe it when other lice treatments have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: Malathion works by attacking the nervous system of lice, which causes them to become paralyzed and die. It contains alcohol, which also helps kill the lice and their eggs on contact. Because it works differently from some other lice treatments, it can be effective even when lice have become resistant to other products.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are scalp irritation, stinging, or a burning feeling where the lotion is applied. Some people may notice redness or minor skin irritation. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: This medicine is flammable — keep it away from open flames, cigarettes, and heat sources while it is on your hair and until your hair is fully dry. Do not use it on children under 6 years old. Avoid getting it in your eyes; if this happens, rinse thoroughly with water. Do not swallow this medication — it is for external use only. If you accidentally swallow it or have signs of a serious reaction (difficulty breathing, seizures, or excessive sweating), seek emergency help immediately. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using it.
typical_dosing: Apply enough lotion to thoroughly wet dry hair and scalp. Leave it on for 8 to 12 hours, then rinse off with shampoo. Do not use a hair dryer. If live lice are still seen after 7 to 9 days, a second treatment may be applied. Only use as directed by your doctor — do not use it more often than prescribed.
